method: Built-in image generation, medical teaching illustration

assets.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: Portrait medical atlas illustration used in an interactive spinal cord atlas. Generate ONE finished portrait image, approximately 1024 x 1536, no montage.
Primary request: A realistic anatomical illustration of the adult human spinal cord, conus medullaris, cauda equina and representative bilateral spinal nerve roots inside a posteriorly opened vertebral canal, from upper cervical spine to sacrum, with delicate cream vertebrae framing the central tissue. Illustration, not a clinical photograph.
Composition: Posterior view, superior at top, full length centered with generous quiet ivory margins. The complete neural tissue and sacrum fit in frame. Central cord is visible uninterrupted. Vertebral posterior arches have been removed in a clean anatomical cutaway; body contours and small residual bone cross-sections at the sides give real depth. Clear cervical and lumbosacral enlargements of the cord. The cord ENDS in a narrow conus at the UPPER lumbar vertebral level around L1-L2, approximately 58% down the image. Below this point show long separate descending slender yellow nerve roots forming the cauda equina in the roomy lumbar/sacral canal, and a subtle thin central filum. Do NOT draw a thick spinal cord continuing into the sacrum.
Roots: use a limited representative set of delicate paired root bundles exiting bilaterally through side gaps. Upper roots roughly lateral, lower roots increasingly descending. The count is intentionally representative, not an exact 31-pair diagram. Show no brain, no skull, no pelvis outside the sacrum, no arteries or pathology.
Style: contemporary high quality medical textbook plate, lifelike three dimensional volume, organic smooth tapering contours, fine soft tissue detail, subtle ivory trabecular bone cut edges, warm muted pink cord, pale ochre roots, no harsh saturated region coloring. Diffuse upper-left lighting, gentle ambient shadows, fine painterly realism, clean warm ivory background matching #f4f3ed.
Text: none. No labels, no arrows, no captions, no numbers, no borders, no logo, no watermark, no signature. All educational labels and selection buttons are added separately in code.
Anatomical invariants: spinal cord shorter than vertebral column; cauda equina comprises roots below the conus. Enlargements occur before the conus, never within the cauda equina. Avoid string-like cord, perfect cylindrical tube, faceted bones or flat cartoon polygons.
assets.limitations: Representative nerve exits; not a 31-pair count, dermatome map or exact segment-to-vertebra conversion. Regions selected by illustrative points, not measured boundaries.

assets.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: One realistic medical atlas illustration for an interactive anatomy page, landscape approximately 1536 x 1152. No montage, no surrounding UI.
Primary request: Adult human spinal cord transverse section viewed from caudal, with posterior/dorsal at the top and anterior/ventral at the bottom. Realistic painterly medical textbook rendering with a small subtle oblique thickness for volume, but the anatomical relationships remain those of an axial cross-section. It is a schematic anatomical illustration, not a specimen photograph.
Composition: Main cord and concentric coverings centered around 40% image width, 51% height. The cord occupies about 34% image width and 43% height, with gently oval organic contour, an anterior median fissure at bottom, narrow dorsal horns at top and broad ventral horns at bottom. White matter is pale cream around a soft gray-rose H-shaped gray matter core connected by a gray commissure containing ONE tiny central canal. The anterior fissure is a normal notch, not a second central canal. Render the gray matter as neural tissue with fine subtle organic mottled texture.
Meninges outside-in: a thin but clearly visible tough pearly blue-gray DURAMATER as the outer sleeve; immediately inside a delicate translucent ARACHNOID membrane; a wider pale blue fluid-filled SUBARACHNOID SPACE with a sparse few fine trabeculae; a very thin warm rose PIA layer touching the cord contour. These three membranes are separate. Do not show fluid between dura and arachnoid. Any expanded thickness is for educational clarity. Show no bones, no arteries and no extra membrane layers.
Nerves on the image RIGHT: several upper/dorsal ochre rootlets emerging from the dorsolateral cord gather into a dorsal sensory root. It passes through one distinct oval dorsal root ganglion at around 73% width, 34% height. Separate lower/ventral rootlets emerge from the anterolateral cord, join into the thinner ventral root, and this ventral root has NO swelling or ganglion. The dorsal root distal to its ganglion and ventral root join outside the meninges at around 83% width, 55% height into one short thick mixed spinal nerve. That short nerve bifurcates at far right into a thin branch directed upward (posterior ramus) and a thicker branch directed downward (anterior ramus). Show a short shared trunk before the split. All rootlets, roots, ganglion and two rami are anatomically continuous, no disconnected branches, no imaginary extra ganglia. The left side may show short paired roots cropped only after their exit, but no ganglion needed there; preferably keep left roots modest.
Style: contemporary precise medical atlas plate with organic contours, subtle lifelike volume, fine clean fibers, muted ochre nerves, warm cream white matter, soft rose-gray gray matter, understated teal/bluish translucent coverings. Gentle upper-left light and soft grounding shadows, warm ivory #f4f3ed background, enough quiet margin around the main cutaway for code-added labels.
Text: none. No baked in labels, numbers, arrows, letters, caption, border, watermark, logo or signature.
Avoid flat cartoon circles, generic nested donuts, perfectly mirrored horns, extra central cavities, artificial chunky nerve cables. The cortical-looking fine details must remain subtle, no histological claims or microscopic axon drawings.
assets.repairPrompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / scientific-educational.
Edit ONLY the outer meningeal envelope at the bottom/anterior midline of this illustration.
Preserve the entire cord, H-shaped gray matter with ONE tiny central canal, anterior median fissure within the cord, posterior horns, all right dorsal rootlets, the dorsal root ganglion, the un-swollen ventral root, mixed nerve and its two rami. Preserve framing, colors, fine medical illustration quality, background and all other structures.
Correction required: The outer DURAMATER must form a smooth continuous gently convex sleeve bridging across the anterior/bottom midline at six o'clock. The ARACHNOID just inside it must also bridge smoothly there. They MUST NOT indent upward into the anterior median fissure of the cord. Remove the current deep notch in the OUTER sleeve at the bottom. The fluid-filled subarachnoid space continues across this bottom region between the smooth arachnoid and the pia-covered cord. Only the very thin PIA touching the neural tissue can follow the cord's anterior median fissure. The fissure inside the cord remains unchanged and visible as a narrow notch, separate from the ONE tiny central canal. Do not add any second canal or cavity in the gray matter.
Keep all neural tissue geometry and nerve paths exactly unchanged, this is a localized repair of the bottom meningeal contour only. No text, no arrows, no labels, no numbers, no watermark, no logo or signature.
assets.limitations: Illustrated transverse organization. Textures, separations and thicknesses are educational, not microscopy or measured anatomy. No particular medullary level is assigned.

review: Cord ends above the cauda equina; representative roots continue below conus.
Dura and arachnoid have a continuous external contour across the anterior midline after localized correction.
One central canal in gray commissure, thinner posterior and wider anterior horns.
One dorsal root ganglion; ventral root without ganglion; roots unite into a mixed nerve before two rami.
No embedded text, logos, signatures or watermarks.
